subject: physics
title: Scalars and vectors
key_idea: A scalar has size only. A vector has size and direction. Distance and speed are scalars. Displacement and velocity are vectors, and so are force, weight and acceleration. A vector is drawn as an arrow.

blocks.text: Every physical quantity is either a scalar or a vector. This section covers the difference and the quantities you need to sort.

items.meaning: A quantity with magnitude only. It has no direction.
A quantity with magnitude and a direction.

blocks.text: Acceleration and momentum are also vectors.

diagram.alt: Sort ten quantities into scalars and vectors.
diagram.prompt: Sort each quantity into scalar or vector.

items: Both scalars and vectors have a size.
Only a vector also has a direction.
Force, weight, acceleration and momentum are vectors.

blocks.text: Motion gives two pairs of quantities. In each pair, one is a scalar and one is a vector.

rows: How far an object moves, along its path
The straight-line distance from the start point to the finish point, with its direction
How fast an object moves, with no direction
The speed of an object in a given direction

blocks.text: Worked idea: a lap of a track

items: A toy car goes once around a circular track and stops where it started.
Its **distance** is the length of the track.
Its **displacement** is zero, because the finish is the same as the start.
Its speed can stay the same, but its velocity changes because its direction keeps changing.

blocks.text: (Higher tier) Motion in a circle has constant speed but changing velocity. A force towards the centre changes the direction of motion but not the speed.

items: Distance and speed have no direction. Displacement and velocity do.
Displacement is measured in a straight line from start to finish.
Changing direction changes the velocity, even at constant speed.

blocks.text: A vector can be shown as an arrow. The arrow carries both parts of the vector.

items: The **length** of the arrow shows the magnitude.
The **direction** the arrow points shows the direction of the vector.
A force of 20 N is drawn twice as long as a force of 10 N.
Weight is drawn as an arrow because it is a vector.
Arrow direction shows the direction of the vector.

checks.q: Describe what is meant by a vector quantity and a scalar quantity.
checks.a: A vector quantity has magnitude and a direction. A scalar quantity has magnitude only.

checks.q: A runner completes one full lap of a 400 m track. State the distance and the displacement.
checks.a: The distance is 400 m. The displacement is 0 m, because the runner finishes at the start point.

checks.q: Which two of these are scalar quantities: displacement, distance, force, speed, velocity?

exam_phrases: velocity is a vector and speed is a scalar
this changes the direction of motion (but not the speed)

mistakes.wrong: Distance is a vector because it can be measured in a direction.
mistakes.right: Distance is a scalar because it has magnitude only. Displacement is the vector.

mistakes.wrong: The Earth's gravitational force makes the Hubble Space Telescope speed up or slow down as it orbits.
mistakes.right: The force makes it accelerate towards the Earth. This changes the direction of motion but not the speed, so the velocity changes.

mistakes.wrong: A stone falling with no air resistance has a constant velocity because it falls in a straight line.
mistakes.right: The magnitude of the velocity increases uniformly and the direction stays constant.

worked_example.question: The speed cameras determine the average speed of cars on the road. The average speed of a car between the cameras and the average velocity of the car between the cameras are different. Explain why.
answer_points: Velocity is a vector and speed is a scalar. Velocity includes direction and speed does not.
So the direction changes, which means the velocity changes.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the vector and scalar link, one for the road not being straight, one for direction changing the velocity.

mistakes.wrong: Scalars have only direction and vectors have size and mass.
mistakes.right: Vectors have size and direction. Scalars have only size. The words must go in the right order.

mistakes.wrong: Magnitude is not an acceptable word for how big a scalar is.
mistakes.right: Size and magnitude are both accepted.

worked_example.question: Use words from the box to complete the sentences below. Words: direction, energy, mass, size. Vectors have size and ______. Scalars have only ______.
worked_example.tip: The answers are only accepted in the given order. Size can also be written as magnitude.

exam_phrases: velocity does take direction into account
displacement depends on direction from start point

mistakes.wrong: The velocity of the toy car is different from its speed because velocity is calculated using distance.
mistakes.right: Speed is calculated using distance. Velocity is calculated using displacement, which takes direction into account.

mistakes.wrong: Distance depends on direction from the start point.
mistakes.right: Distance does not depend on direction from the start point. Displacement does.

worked_example.question: A toy car travels around a race track. After one lap it is back at the start position. Explain why the velocity of the toy car is different from its speed as it travels around the track.
answer_points: Speed is a scalar and velocity is a vector.
Velocity takes direction into account and speed does not.
Or: speed is calculated using distance, but velocity is calculated using displacement.
worked_example.tip: Any two of the marking points score. The answer must be about direction.
